[00:16] Alex Chen: Great, thanks. I�m Alex, AE, and with me is Priya our SE and Jordan on solutions. Today we�re gonna walk through the model catalog — how customers pick open models, look at benchmarks and compatibility matrices, and where Redwood Optimize and Console fit into the POC.

[00:48] Sara Lee: Our primary ask is low-latency chat summarization and clinical note generation; we�re evaluating open models because of cost and data control.

[01:02] Jordan Lee: first, model catalog: we surface curated open models — small, medium, large families — with redwood-verified perf profiles. each entry has throughput, median p50 and p95 latency per token, and quality evals on common prompt sets.
[01:20] Derek Wu: How accurate are those latencies? our seq lengths vary a lot — some notes are 800 tokens.
[01:27] Priya Nair: good question. benchmarks are run across our standard sequence buckets (<=256, 256-1024, >1024). for long sequences we call out KV cache benefits and recommend compaction/quant profiles. p95 for a 13B quantized model on an A100 usually sits in the 150-220ms range for <=256, but for >1024 it bumps — depends on batch and prefix cache hit rate.
[01:52] Michael Ortiz: you mentioned quant profiles — do you support int8 or int4 quant?
[01:56] Priya Nair: we support several quant variants; int8 is the most common for production. int4 is available for certain models and yields bigger cost savings but watch for quality regressions — Redwood Optimize has preflight tests that run your prompt sets and recommend the best quant/profile combo.
[02:18] Anita Gomez: on the security side we�re looking for KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC-only. how does Redwood Private handle key management?
[02:25] Alex Chen: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM through the private control plane; audit logs are exportable and retained per contract. we can share the SOC2 pack after the call.
[02:36] Sara Lee: can the catalog show which models are allowed for private deployments?
[02:39] Jordan Lee: yes, each model entry has a compatibility matrix: hardware (A100, H100, T4), quant support (yes/no), private deploy support (yes/no), and recommended memory footprint. you can filter the catalog in Console by those attributes.
[02:54] Derek Wu: what about on-prem? some of our nodes are on-prem with older GPUs.
[02:58] Priya Nair: we have an on-prem package; the compatibility matrix flags models that run with reduced perf on older cards. also the runtime has kernel selection heuristics to pick best path. sometimes you trade throughput for compatibility.
[03:12] Michael Ortiz: talk to me about throughput vs latency vs cost — we care about cost per 1k tokens mostly.
[03:18] Priya Nair: simple rule: bigger models raise latency and cost but often increase answer quality. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and caching policies to reduce unit cost while meeting latency SLOs. e.g., for reply generation we often configure continuous batching with a 20ms max wait and prefix KV cache; that brought down per-token cost 18-25% in our bench.
[03:38] Alex Chen: we�ve got some example numbers in the spreadsheet. for a 7B int8 model on Dedicated A100, p50 token latency ~20-30ms and cost X; 13B int8 p50 of ~40-60ms. p95 varies more.
